<a id="actionargsvalidation"></a>

## `ActionArgsValidation`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.ActionArgsValidation` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The schema step of the action runner: checks one call's arguments against the action's parameters before anything is gated or run. Immutable result.

- Every argument must be a declared parameter (case-insensitive); unknown names are refused so a misspelt argument never silently does nothing.
- A required parameter must be given and not null; an optional one given as null counts as absent.
- Types: a [`ActionValueKind.String`](#actionvaluekind--string) takes any value (numbers and booleans are read as invariant text); [`ActionValueKind.Integer`](#actionvaluekind--integer) a whole number or text that parses; [`ActionValueKind.Number`](#actionvaluekind--number) any number or text that parses; [`ActionValueKind.Boolean`](#actionvaluekind--boolean) true/false or the text true, false, 1, 0. Console and script arguments arrive as text, API arguments as JSON values: both pass the same rules.
- Allowed values (case-insensitive) and inclusive bounds are checked.
- No problem message repeats a value: arguments may be private (a note's text), and the message reaches the audit line and the caller.

### `string ActionName { get; }`

The action the arguments were checked against; empty for the shared "valid" answer.

<a id="actionaudit"></a>

## `ActionAudit`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.ActionAudit` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The `ACTION` audit line: what ran, for whom, how it ended - and never the player's text (envelope privacy rule: ids, counts and lengths only).

**Redaction.** An argument value is shown only when it belongs to a declared parameter that is not [`ActionParameter.IsPrivate`](#actionparameter--isprivate) and, on a [`ActionTier.Write`](#actiontier--write) action, is not text. Everything else - private and Write-tier text, undeclared names, every value of a name no action has - prints as `<private:N>` (N = characters). A Write-tier handler's own message is replaced by its length too, because it may quote what was written.

**Where.** Act and Write calls, and every refusal or failure of any tier, are console lines (tag `ACTION`; failed, timed-out and late ones at Warn). A Read call that worked is trace-file only (`action/run`), so a client polling state cannot flood the console.

What an action is: its name, tier, arguments and whether it destroys something. The registry, the console (`act list`), the API catalog (`/v1/actions`) and API clients all read this one description. Immutable.

<a id="actionfamilyattribute"></a>

## `ActionFamilyAttribute`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.ActionFamilyAttribute` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Base: `Attribute`

Marks a framework class as an action family: the runtime finds it in the framework's assemblies on the first frame, creates it once and calls [`IActionFamily.Register`](#iactionfamily--register). Adding a family is adding a file - no init line, no edit to a shared file. The class implements [`IActionFamily`](#iactionfamily) and has a parameterless constructor (any visibility).

Only assemblies named `CwyLs.ModLoader*` are searched. Code mods publish their actions with `helper.Actions.Register` instead. Keep the constructor and static fields free of game calls: families are created before the room exists; resolve game services inside handlers.

<a id="actionfamilyattribute--ctor"></a>

### `ActionFamilyAttribute(string family)`

Marks the class as the family `family`.

**Parameters**

- `family`: The family name, e.g. `music`: every action it registers is named `<family>.<verb>`.

<a id="actionfamilyattribute--family"></a>

### `string Family { get; }`

The family name.

<a id="actiongate"></a>

## `ActionGate`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.ActionGate` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The default tier gating every action goes through before its handler runs. Pure, so the table below is unit-tested.

- **Read tier**: Allow, every caller
- **API caller, Act or Write, `[Api] AllowActions=false`**: Deny
- **Write tier, `[Data] AllowWrites=false`**: Deny
- **Destructive (a delete), any caller**: Confirm
- **Write tier from the API**: Confirm
- **everything else**: Allow

A Confirm verdict with no confirmation dialog installed ends as Declined: [`DenyingConfirmationGate`](#denyingconfirmationgate) never approves.

**Returns:** The verdict and its reason.

<a id="actionrunner"></a>

## `ActionRunner`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.ActionRunner` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Implements: [`IActionRunner`](#iactionrunner)

The action runner: look up → check the arguments against the schema ([`ActionArgsValidation`](#actionargsvalidation)) → tier gate ([`ActionGate`](#actiongate) with the live switches from [`ActionServices.GateSettings`](#actionservices--gatesettings)) → in-game confirmation when the gate asks for one ([`ActionServices.ConfirmationGate`](#actionservices--confirmationgate)) → hop to the main thread through the shared dispatcher with the caller's timeout → the handler → one `ACTION` audit record. Every outcome is an [`ActionResult`](#actionresult); the runner never throws and never faults.

- **Timeouts.** [`ActionRequest.Timeout`](#actionrequest--timeout) bounds the main-thread hop only (null → [`ActionRunner.DefaultTimeout`](#actionrunner--defaulttimeout), more than [`ActionRunner.MaxTimeout`](#actionrunner--maxtimeout) is cut to it, zero or less is InvalidArgs). The confirmation has its own limit ([`ConfirmationRequest.DefaultTimeout`](#confirmationrequest--defaulttimeout); no answer = no).
- **Late handlers.** A handler that started before the limit but finished after it is reported to the caller as TimedOut and gets a second audit record marked late with its real outcome, so the audit never claims that something which ran did not.
- **Owners.** A mod caller's work runs in that mod's dispatcher lane (`mod:<id>`, budgeted, dropped when the mod stops); everything else under [`ActionRunner.Owner`](#actionrunner--owner) in the framework lane.
- **Never block on the main thread.** The hop is always queued, so a main-thread caller that waits synchronously for the task stalls until the timeout and gets TimedOut. Await it or continue from it (the console, scripts and mods do).

<a id="actionrunner--ctor"></a>

### `ActionRunner(ActionRegistry registry, IActionDispatcher dispatcher, ActionServices services, Action<ActionAuditRecord> audit = null)`

Creates a runner.

**Parameters**

- `registry`: Where actions are looked up ([`ActionRegistry.Shared`](#actionregistry--shared) in game).
- `dispatcher`: The main-thread hop.
- `services`: The gate switches, the confirmation gate and the error sink ([`ActionServices.Shared`](#actionservices--shared) in game).
- `audit`: Receives one record per finished call (and one more per late handler); [`ActionAudit.Publish`](#actionaudit--publish) in game. Null for none.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: A required argument is null.

<a id="actionrunner--defaulttimeout"></a>

The main-thread hop's limit when the request names none (the dispatcher's default).

<a id="actionrunner--maxtimeout"></a>

How an action call ended. Values are explicit and never renumbered (the API reports them).

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|

| <a id="actionstatus--failed"></a>`Failed` | 1 | It ran and failed (the game refused, a handler threw). |

| <a id="actionstatus--declined"></a>`Declined` | 5 | The player said no in the in-game confirmation, or the confirmation could not be shown; nothing ran. |

<a id="actiontoolschema"></a>

## `ActionToolSchema`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.ActionToolSchema` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

An action as a tool an LLM or MCP client can call (a mod, an MCP server, `/v1/actions`): name, one-line description, tier hints and a JSON-schema object for the arguments. Pure: the result is plain dictionaries and lists that any JSON writer (for example `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.JsonWriter`) can serialise.

Shape (keys in this order):

```csharp
{ "name": "music.play", "description": "...", "tier": "act", "readOnly": false, "destructive": false,
  "inputSchema": { "type": "object",
                   "properties": { "title": { "type": "string", "description": "...", "enum": [...] },
                                   "volume": { "type": "number", "description": "...", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1 } },
                   "required": [ "title" ],
                   "additionalProperties": false } }
```

`readOnly`/`destructive` map onto MCP's `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint`. `additionalProperties: false` matches the runner, which refuses unknown arguments.

The text forms of actions shared by the console (`act list|run`) and scripts (`cwy.do music.play title=Rain`): reading `key=value` words, and listing and printing actions. Pure.

<a id="actionwords--usage"></a>

**Parameters**

<a id="actionwords--formatlist"></a>

<a id="actionwords--parseargs"></a>

### `static ActionWordsResult ParseArgs(IReadOnlyList<string> words, int start = 0)`

Reads `key=value` words into arguments, from index `start`. The first `=` splits a word, so a value may contain `=`; an empty value is the empty text. Quotes are the tokenizer's job (the console's `CommandLineParser`), so `title="Rain on glass"` arrives as one word. Values stay text: the runner's schema step reads numbers and booleans from text in invariant culture.

**Parameters**

- `words`: The words; null means none.
- `start`: The first word to read.

**Returns:** The arguments, or the problem (a word without `=`, a blank or repeated name).

## `DenyingConfirmationGate`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.DenyingConfirmationGate` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Implements: [`IConfirmationGate`](#iconfirmationgate)

The gate before the in-game dialog exists: it never approves. Every request ends as [`ConfirmationOutcome.Unavailable`](#confirmationoutcome--unavailable) at once, so a Confirm verdict can never turn into a silent yes.

<a id="denyingconfirmationgate--reason"></a>

<a id="denyingconfirmationgate--instance"></a>

The one instance.

<a id="denyingconfirmationgate--confirmasync"></a>

### `Task<ConfirmationResult> ConfirmAsync(ConfirmationRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)`

Shows the question and completes when the player answers, the request times out ([`ConfirmationRequest.Timeout`](#confirmationrequest--timeout): timeout means no), or the token is cancelled. Called from any thread; the implementation owns the main-thread hop. Never faults: a failure to show the dialog is [`ConfirmationOutcome.Unavailable`](#confirmationoutcome--unavailable).

**Parameters**

- `request`: What to ask.
- `cancellationToken`: Stops waiting (counts as not approved).

**Returns:** The answer.

<a id="iactiondispatcher"></a>

## `IActionDispatcher`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.IActionDispatcher` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The main-thread hop the runner uses: the shared dispatcher in the game (`CwyLs.ModLoader.Threading.MainThread.InvokeAsync`), a `MainThreadQueue` in tests.

<a id="iactiondispatcher--invokeasync"></a>

### `Task<ActionResult> InvokeAsync(string owner, string label, Func<ActionResult> work, TimeSpan timeout, CancellationToken cancellationToken)`

Runs `work` on the main thread and completes with its result. Always queued (awaiting it on the main thread cannot deadlock).

**Parameters**

- `owner`: The dispatcher owner: `mod:<id>` for a mod caller, the runner's own owner otherwise.
- `label`: What the work is, for the dispatcher's logs.
- `work`: The handler call.
- `timeout`: The caller's wall-clock limit; work not started by then is skipped.
- `cancellationToken`: Stops the wait and, if not yet started, the work.

**Returns:** The task: the work's result; faulted with `TimeoutException` at the limit, with the dispatcher's refusal (`MainThreadRejectedException`), or with the work's own exception; cancelled when the token fires.

<a id="uiclickpolicy"></a>

## `UiClickPolicy`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.UiClickPolicy` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The deny list of `UiClick.Invoke` (project rule: never touch the shop, account linking, cloud sync, SNS or the browser). Pure, so every rule is unit-tested.

**Words.** Every segment of a hierarchy path is split into lower-case words at separators and case changes (`InquiryIDButton` → inquiry, id, button; `SNS` → sns) and a click is refused when any segment holds a denied word. Whole words only, so `CloudyButton` (weather) stays clickable while `SaveDataUploadInterval` does not. The words were chosen against the game's RoomScene (game 1.17.3), e.g. `…/UI_FacilitySetting/SNS/Discord`, `…/PC_Account_Setting/…/LinkButton`, `…/General/…/SaveDataUploadInterval`, `…/UI_FacilityEnviroment/…/ShopButton`, `…/General/…/FAQ/TitleText/FAQButton`.

**Types.** The game adapter adds the exact component types that open these areas (the account-transfer dialog, purchase popover, hyperlinks, ...); a click is refused when the control or any ancestor carries one ([`UiClickPolicy.CheckTypes`](#uiclickpolicy--checktypes)).

<a id="uiclickpolicy--account"></a>

### `const string Account = "account"`

Category of account sign-in, linking and transfer controls.

<a id="uiclickpolicy--cloudsync"></a>

### `const string CloudSync = "cloud sync"`

Category of cloud save and upload controls.

<a id="uiclickpolicy--shop"></a>

### `const string Shop = "shop"`

Category of shop and purchase controls.

<a id="uiclickpolicy--snsbrowser"></a>

### `const string SnsBrowser = "sns/browser"`

Category of controls that open SNS pages or the web browser.

<a id="uiclickpolicy--deniedwords"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair<string, string>> DeniedWords { get; }`

Every denied word and its category, sorted by word.

<a id="uiclickpolicy--checkname"></a>

### `static UiClickVerdict CheckName(string name, string where)`

Checks one name's words.

**Parameters**

- `name`: A object or type name.
- `where`: How to name it in the reason.

<a id="uiclickpolicy--checkpath"></a>

### `static UiClickVerdict CheckPath(string path)`

Checks every segment of a `Root/Child/Leaf` hierarchy path.

**Parameters**

- `path`: The path; null or blank is allowed (nothing to match).

<a id="uiclickpolicy--checktypes"></a>

### `static UiClickVerdict CheckTypes(IEnumerable<string> typeFullNames, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> deniedTypes)`

Checks component types against an exact deny list (full names, ordinal).

**Parameters**

- `typeFullNames`: The full names of the components on the control and its ancestors.
- `deniedTypes`: Full name → category, supplied by the game adapter.

<a id="uiclickpolicy--tokens"></a>

Splits a name into lower-case words: at any character that is not a letter or digit, and at case and digit boundaries (`UI_FacilitySetting` → ui, facility, setting; `SNSButton` → sns, button; `Cook(B)Button` → cook, b, button).

**Parameters**
